source: [R4575]; weights from https://github.com/pavanvyn/quadruple-stability, mlp_model_3p1_ghost_v1.2.2.pkl (read 2026-10-30 without running its code, scripts/build_quadruple_stability.py)

stable_below.basis: classify_quad_3p1.py of the authors: a system is stable when the network's probability of 'unstable' is below 0.5

q_in_min.basis: paper section 3.1: masses log-uniform over one order of magnitude, so the inner mass ratio m2/m1 is at least 0.1

q_mid_max.basis: the help text of classify_quad_3p1.py: 'best if < ~3'; the paper's masses give m3/(m1+m2) up to 5 but the authors say to stay under about 3

q_out_max.basis: the help text of classify_quad_3p1.py: 'best if < ~2'

eccentricity_max.basis: paper section 3.1: eccentricities uniform from 0 to 0.95

outer_orbits.basis: paper section 2: 'stable' means bound and not chaotic over 100 outer orbits (a ghost run with the inner axis larger by 1e-6 au diverging by less than 1e-2 in the inner axis), not stable for a stellar lifetime

divergence_limit.basis: paper section 2: delta(t) = (a_orig - a_ghost) / a_orig above 1e-2 at any step is unstable

axis_margin.basis: GEN.1016: a system the network calls stable is accepted only if it is still stable with both axis ratios a_in/a_mid and a_mid/a_out multiplied by this number (the hierarchy made looser). Hand-tuned on the 331 REBOUND systems of GEN.1029 (the paper's labelling rule): the plain network was right on 18 of its 33 stable calls (precision 0.55), at 1.3 on 8 of 9 (0.89, the paper reports 0.91) with recall 0.42 of the truly stable ones; 1.5 gave 5 of 5 with recall 0.26

fallback_margin.basis: GM7: outside the network's documented range both nested triples must pass at this multiple of the required axis ratio and the verdict is flagged lower confidence; on 4e4 coplanar systems against the network it gave precision 0.78 and recall 0.53 (1.0 gave 0.74 and 0.98)

level_margin.basis: GM8: the multiple of the required axis ratio a nested-triple test at one level of a deeper tree must clear; 1.0 (none) because the nested test is right for 88 percent of 2+2 systems ([R4575: Table 3]) and the 2+2 network is not ported
